reference_sql:
WITH period_lines AS (
  -- one row per order line of an order placed from 7 to 20 April 2025 (UTC days of order_ts)
  SELECT l.order_line_id, l.promo_id
  FROM order_lines l
  JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = l.order_id
  WHERE o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-04-07 00:00:00'
    AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-04-21 00:00:00'
), with_promo AS (
  -- one row per order line, with its promotion's name (missing when the line had none)
  SELECT w.order_line_id, p.promo_name
  FROM period_lines w
  LEFT JOIN promotions p ON p.promo_id = w.promo_id
), counts AS (
  -- one row: the row count before and after the join
  SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM period_lines) AS lines_before,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM with_promo) AS rows_after
)
SELECT lines_before, rows_after,
  rows_after - lines_before AS added_rows
FROM counts

WITH joined AS (
  -- one row per order line and matching promotion: the join being checked
  SELECT l.order_line_id, p.promo_name
  FROM order_lines l
  JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = l.order_id
  LEFT JOIN promotions p ON p.promo_id = l.promo_id
  WHERE o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-04-07 00:00:00'
    AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-04-21 00:00:00'
)
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT order_line_id) AS lines_before, COUNT(*) AS rows_after,
  COUNT(*) - COUNT(DISTINCT order_line_id) AS added_rows
FROM joined

WITH period_lines AS (
  -- one row per order line of an order placed from 7 to 20 April 2025 (UTC days of order_ts)
  SELECT l.order_line_id, l.promo_id
  FROM order_lines l
  JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = l.order_id
  WHERE o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-04-07 00:00:00'
    AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-04-21 00:00:00'
), with_promo AS (
  -- one row per order line, with its promotion's name (missing when the line had none)
  SELECT w.order_line_id, p.promo_name
  FROM period_lines w
  LEFT JOIN promotions p ON p.promo_id = w.promo_id
), before_count AS (
  -- one row: the lines before the join
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS lines_before FROM period_lines
), after_count AS (
  -- one row: the rows after it
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_after FROM with_promo
)
SELECT b.lines_before, a.rows_after, a.rows_after - b.lines_before AS added_rows
FROM before_count b
CROSS JOIN after_count a

other_way.sql:
WITH joined AS (
  -- one row per order line and matching promotion: the join being checked
  SELECT l.order_line_id, p.promo_name
  FROM order_lines l
  JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = l.order_id
  LEFT JOIN promotions p ON p.promo_id = l.promo_id
  WHERE o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-04-07 00:00:00'
    AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-04-21 00:00:00'
)
SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT order_line_id) AS lines_before, COUNT(*) AS rows_after,
  COUNT(*) - COUNT(DISTINCT order_line_id) AS added_rows
FROM joined
other_way.tradeoff: Counting distinct line IDs after the join checks the grain in one step, but it trusts order_line_id to be unique.

solver.query:
WITH ls AS (
  SELECT ol.order_line_id, ol.promo_id
  FROM order_lines ol JOIN orders o ON o.order_id = ol.order_id
  WHERE o.order_ts >= TIMESTAMP '2025-04-07 00:00:00' AND o.order_ts < TIMESTAMP '2025-04-21 00:00:00'
), j AS (
  SELECT ls.order_line_id, p.promo_name
  FROM ls LEFT JOIN promotions p ON p.promo_id = ls.promo_id
)
SELECT (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ls) AS lines_before, (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM j) AS rows_after,
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM j) - (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ls) AS added_rows
